title: Bond Market Update: 03-Jan-19 03:21 ET
text:
The market at 15:21 ET 10-Year: +31/32....+1 31/32%.... GNMAs: .... USD/JPY: 107.53.... EUR/USD: 1.1399 Apple's guidance cut weighs on investor sentiment
-- 7:00 ET: MBA Mortgage Index for the past two weeks (actual -8.5%; prior -5.8%)
-- 8:15 ET: December ADP Employment Change ( actual 271K 170K; prior 179K)
-- 8:30 ET: Weekly Initial Claims ( actual 231K 220K; prior 221K) and Continuing Claims ( actual 1740K ; prior 1708K)
-- 10:00 ET: December ISM Manufacturing Index ( actual 54.1 57.8; prior 59.3) +31/32..+1 31/32%.. USD/JPY: 107.53.. EUR/USD: 1.1399
Continued Growth Worries Lift Treasuries U.S. Treasuries ended Thursday on a sharply higher note with the long bond adding almost two points while the 10-yr note gained nearly a point. The Treasury complex spiked after yesterday's cash close, responding to Apple's (AAPL 142.26, -15.67) first revenue guidance cut since 2002, which was blamed on weak demand in China. The early-evening rally in Treasuries was not due to Apple per se. Instead, it resulted from a concern that Apple is not an isolated case and that other companies will have to tone down expectations of their own. The market received a ADP Employment Change report (actual 217K 170K) ahead of tomorrow's release of the Employment Situation report from the BLS, but growth concerns were brought back to the forefront after the ISM Manufacturing Index for December (actual 54.1% 57.8%) missed expectations with the New Orders component surrendering its entire spike from November. Treasuries accelerated their advance in the wake of the report, ending the session on their highs. The final push into the close pressured the 2-yr yield beneath the effective fed funds rate, which stands at 2.40%. Today' session not only saw a decrease in rate hike expectations, but the market is starting to give somewhat serious thought to before the end of the year. The implied probability of a rate cut in December jumped to 46.1% from just 9.6% yesterday. Fed Chairman Jay Powell will speak tomorrow at 10:15 ET and his remarks will be watched closely for signs of a change to the Fed's outlook. Yield Check: 2-yr: -11 bps to 2.38% 3-yr: -12 bps to 2.34% 5-yr: -13 bps to 2.37% 10-yr: -11 bps to 2.55% 30-yr: -8 bps to 2.90% News: The Department of State issued a travel advisory, warning citizens traveling to China to exercise increased caution due to "arbitrary enforcement of local laws." White House Council of Economic Advisers Chair Kevin Hassett said he expects more companies with exposure to China to follow in Apple's footsteps, cutting their guidance. The U.S. Treasury will auction $38 billion in 3-yr notes on Tuesday at 13:00 ET. The sale will be followed by a $24 billion 10-yr note reopening on Wednesday and a $16 billion 30-yr bond reopening on Thursday. British Prime Minister Theresa May was scheduled to meet with European officials today, including EU Council President Donald Tusk, German Chancellor Angela Merkel, and Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte. Ms. May is seeking to secure concessions regarding the Irish border ahead of the Brexit withdrawal bill vote expected during the week of January 14. Nikkei reported that the Bank of Japan may lower its forecast for consumer inflation in 2019 to 1.0% from 1.4% Today's Data: Initial claims for the week ending December 29 increased by 10,000 to 231,000 220,000) from last week's revised reading of 221,000 (from 216,000). Continuing claims for the week ending December 22 increased by 32,000 to 1.740 million from last week's revised reading of 1.708 million (from 1.701 million). The key takeaway from the report is that claims continue hovering within a sideways range that has been maintained since mid-2018. The ISM Manufacturing Index for December decreased to 54.1% 57.8%) from 59.3% in November. The key takeaway from the report is that the December decrease was fueled by a sharp pullback in the New Orders component, which is the same element that lifted the November ISM Manufacturing Index into the neighborhood of its high from 2018. Commodities: WTI crude: +1.7% to $47.16/bbl Gold: +1.1% to $1294.60/ozt
